newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso ends off on neutral cenbank policy.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso ends off on neutral cenbank policy.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed 3.0 lower at 1,015 after the central bank left its forex policy unchanged, failing to take any action to halt the peso's recent rise against the dollar.
"There was a lot of speculation all morning," one interbank dealer said in a telephone interview.

He added that the market calmed down considerably, however, after news reports quoted a central bank spokesman as saying the board of directors adjourned their meeting without making any policy announcement. The central bank said only that it would continue analyzing the peso's movements.

The peso's rise since early June, when it was trading at more than 1,070 to the dollar, has prompted widespread calls from exporters for a devaluation as the rise makes Colombian goods less competitive abroad.
A strong peso also erodes the value of foreign exchange reserves, but the central bank likes a strong peso as a buffer against inflation, which is expected to total more than 21 percent this year.
Dealers reported 438 trades in Friday's session for a total of $177 million and said the peso held in a 1,019.60 to 1,012.40 range.
